messages:
Maya: :rotating_light: Paging — we're seeing a sustained spike in `upstream-io` 5xxs from EU region, started ~08:05 UTC. Customers reporting ingestion failures.
incident-bot: Incident created (INC-2026-0423). Severity: P2. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026-0423
Eli: I'm on it, grabbing logs now. Lina, can you check if any deploys touched the upstream gateway in the last hour?
Lina: no deploys in last 2h. I pulled recent gateway metrics — increased 500_error_ratio across p99 latency windows.
Pat: seeing matching errors in logs: repeated connection reset followed by \"verify_signature failed\" stack. Likely an upstream transient but it's customer-facing.
Maya: initial customer impact assessment: around 12 customer API keys showing >10% error rate in last 10m. Not wide blast but affecting a few heavy tenants.
Eli: suggested live mitigation — suppress noisy alert rule and add a quick richer signature to reduce noise while we triage. I'll handoff to oncall. @oncall-bot please assign to whoever is oncall now.
oncall-bot: Assigned to Pat for 30 minutes.
Pat: oncall ack. Starting with mitigation: propose to change alert threshold from 5xx_rate > 3% over 5m to > 6% for next 15m and add regex exclusion for the known benign reset message.
Maya: agree on temp threshold bump + signature. Need dashboard to track impacted API keys so we can revert precisely — create a short-lived dashboard panel grouping errors by api_key and error_signature.
Eli: putting filter together, example log query to identify signature candidates:
```
index=prod logs | json | where service==\"upstream-io\" | parse message \"*verify_signature*\" as sig | stats count() by api_key, sig | sort -count
```
Pat: here's the regex I want to add to the alert rule to suppress the benign reset noise: \"connection reset by peer.*cause=timeout\" — will test it in the rule simulator first.
Lina: I can spin a canary change in alerting config store. Plan: (1) push rule with new regex as `dry_run=true` for 5m to ensure we don't accidentally mute true positives, (2) if safe, set threshold to 6% with a 15m window, (3) create dashboard panel and share link.
Maya: please include an explicit rollback step after 2 hours or once errors are below baseline for 30m. Document the rationale in the alert change description.
Eli: doing a quick signature search — found two main fingerprints: `verify_signature failed` and `tls_handshake timeout`. The former correlates strongly with customer errors, the latter seems infra. We should only add exclusion for the `tls_handshake timeout` variant if it's confirmed benign.
Pat: test results: rule simulator shows suppression of 42 previously noisy hits and no suppression of the top 6 actual customer failures. Good.
Pat: applying change in canary (config repo commit):
```
commit: alerting/ups-io-5xx-rule.yaml
changes:
  - threshold: 6
  - window: 15m
  - exclusions: [\"connection reset by peer.*cause=timeout\"]
flags: dry_run=true
```
DeployBot: deploy started for alert-configs v3.14.2
DeployBot: deploy success for alert-configs v3.14.2 (canary)
Lina: canary running. Creating dashboard panel now — panels: errors_by_api_key, error_signature_heatmap, p50/p95 latency. Link: https://redwood/dashboards/quick/INC-2026-0423
Maya: sharing with support — ask them to route any reports from impacted API keys to this thread. Also cc: customer success for the 12 tenants.
Eli: monitoring: after canary applied, aggregate error rate for those 12 keys dropped from 11% -> 4.5% over 10m. Looks promising.
Pat: after 20m of canary, no missed alerts for other signatures. Recommend promoting change out of dry_run. Anyone object?
Maya: no objections, go ahead but keep 1hr watch and maintain rollback timer.
Pat: promoting change to global (commit change with dry_run=false):
```
commit: alerting/ups-io-5xx-rule.yaml
changes:
  - threshold: 6
  - window: 15m
  - exclusions: [\"connection reset by peer.*cause=timeout\"]
flags: dry_run=false
rollout: 100% over 5m
canary_note: INC-2026-0423
```
DeployBot: deploy started for alert-configs v3.14.3
DeployBot: deploy success for alert-configs v3.14.3 (global)
Lina: dashboard updated to include a monitor panel that alerts if any api_key has >5% error for 30m — will help detect regressions.
Maya: update customer impact: errors now below baseline for all 12 keys. Sending post to support + CS with incident summary.
Eli: follow-up tasks:
- Pat: add precise test cases and example logs to the alert rule description (so future owners know the intent)
- Lina: keep dashboard for 48h retention and add annotation for the rule change timestamp
- Maya: run a small eval on model-based anomaly detection to ensure we didn't mask slow-spreading regressions
- Eli: schedule a short post-incident retro tomorrow (15m) to decide if the exclusion should be made permanent or replaced with upstream fix.
Pat: noted. I'll open a PR with the tests and update the alert docs.
Maya: thanks all. Marking incident as mitigated — moving to monitoring stage. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring.
Lina: leaving the dashboard link in the incident ticket and adding an owner tag `eng-sre/alerts`.
Eli: one last note — we should also add a short-term synthetic check that hits a set of sample api_keys to detect any silent regressions. I'll file a ticket.
Maya: great. We'll reconvene at the retro. Closing the live-handoff. :mag_right:
